parsed.explanation: No criminalisation, no documented anti-trans violence against visitors, and prosecutorial guidance treating gender-identity hostility as aggravating are genuine protections. Against that: a 2024 cabinet decision and ministry directive to draft a policy banning LGBTQIA+ advocacy/promotion, framing the community as contrary to constitutional and religious values; a heterosexual-only Marriage Act; no SOGI anti-discrimination law; partner protections absent; and a record (one prosecuted case, rarely-invoked guidance) showing thin practical recourse. The operative exposure is state threat-framing plus conservative social climate, not statute or custody exposure. Nothing documents entry bans, document checks, facility exclusion, or detention of visitors. Outing risks confrontation, service refusal, and weak official protection, not imprisonment.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border or document screening targeting trans visitors; no X-marker or mismatch procedure sourced either way.
entry_documents.protection: Same-sex conduct not criminalised; no documented entry refusal of LGBT visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Marriage Act amendment could bear on a partner-based visa or registration query, but this is not sourced.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Cabinet decision and advocacy-ban drafting attach official suspicion to public promotion; a visibly trans visitor has no resident standing to argue the private-conduct distinction. Enforcement form of the policy is not sourced.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No trans-specific criminal offence; prosecutorial guidance directs prosecutors to weigh gender-identity hostility toward prosecution.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If stopped, hostile official framing could compound a stop, but no custody pathway is documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility, ward, custody-placement or strip-search rule documented in either direction.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Absence of evidence is not safety; thin-data jurisdiction, so unresolved rather than affirmatively safe.

care_services.exposure: No SOGI anti-discrimination law means service refusal has no statutory remedy; Family Protection Act excludes same-sex partners.
care_services.protection: Prosecutorial guidance offers recourse only if a crime occurs; Teaching Service and digital-denigration protections do not reach visitors' care.
care_services.interaction: Medical emergency while outed sits in an unregulated space with documented thin enforcement culture.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2024 cabinet decision and justice-ministry directive to ban LGBTQIA+ advocacy/promotion, framed as contrary to constitutional, religious and Christian values — documented state threat-framing aimed at visibility rather than private conduct.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: UN joint statement (2011); Prosecution Policy 2003 and Prosecutors Code 2017 require disregarding sexual preference and treating GI hostility as aggravating.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing at the top coexists with protective guidance mid-institution; churches, officials and chiefs already opposed local advocacy, indicating enforcement sympathy toward the framing.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. A travelling parent accompanying a gender-nonconforming child would face the same conservative climate and absent protections.
minors_guardians.interaction: Advocacy-ban framing could reach visibility by a child in public, but no sourced rule addresses minors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Conservative climate with advice to avoid public displays of affection, no active gay scene, and church/official/chief opposition to LGBT advocacy; only one prosecuted violence case (lesbians) in the record and near-invisible LGBTI court presence — thin recourse if harmed.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented pattern of anti-trans violence against visitors; same-sex conduct legal; prosecutorial guidance directs hostility-based prosecutions.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Guidance is rarely invoked in practice (one case documented), so street hostility would likely meet informal resolution.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No general anti-discrimination protection; Family Protection Act excludes same-sex partners; whether the advocacy-ban policy has been drafted, given legal form, or enforced is unsourced; application rate of prosecutorial guidance unknown; subnational variation unevidenced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Prosecutorial guidance and the Harmful Digital Communications Act 2024 section 2(2)(j) are the concrete, citable levers for a victim.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper guidance plus documented rarity of invocation means remedies exist but rarely operate.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars and registers transgender visitors with routine, near-universally enforced exclusion. This dossier documents no entry bar, register, or visitor-facing state screening — only hostile framing of advocacy. Materially higher than 0.35-A because no universal-exposure mechanism reaches the traveller.

Kestrel Isles shows discretionary border secondary screening with refused admission and slow remedies. This dossier's exposure is official threat-framing plus absent protections rather than documented border friction; comparable uncertainty and friction ceiling, but with an actively hostile state posture on one side and no documented screening on the other. Similar tier, slightly different mix.

Meridia documents trained border officers, written decisions, counsel access and a working tribunal. This dossier lacks those documented protections and adds a 2024 state campaign framing LGBTQIA+ activity as contrary to national values, with proven thin recourse (one prosecuted case). Materially lower than 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a conservative state moving visibly against LGBTQIA+ visibility while leaving private conduct legal. The traveller-facing exposure is official threat-framing (a cabinet decision and ministry directive targeting advocacy and promotion) plus a social climate advising concealment, filtered through institutions whose protective machinery — prosecutorial guidance on gender-identity hostility — is documented as rarely invoked. Nothing documents border screening, facility exclusion, custody placement, or violence against visitors, so no tier-1 or tier-2 exposure is established; unknowns are thin-data questions, not evidenced harms. The advocacy-ban's legal form and enforcement are unsourced, capping severity. Net: outing brings social hostility, service-refusal with no statutory remedy, and unreliable official protection, but no credible imprisonment pathway — Elevated Risk, upper half.
